dek: A Las Vegas betting radio veteran who sold picks through Sportsmemo and his own RobVenoSports.com before joining WagerTalk in 2020. Passes run from $39 for a day to $1,999 for a year. The guarantee pays in site credit, the records on show are runs chosen by the seller, and we found no buyer posts about him either way.

short_answer: Rob Veno is a real, long running name in Las Vegas betting media. His WagerTalk bio says he started co hosting a betting radio show in 1992, was part of Sportsmemo radio from 1998 and joined WagerTalk in the summer of 2020. A saved copy of his own site, RobVenoSports.com, shows it selling his plays from a Denver mailing address around 2020. Today he sells through WagerTalk, a Las Vegas pick marketplace with written terms and a street address. In that narrow sense the service is legitimate.

Whether his picks make money over time is a separate question, and nothing we could open answers it. The sales copy leads with runs such as "CFB + NFL L9W = +71.7 units, 59.7% (83-56-0)" and "NFL Playoffs L3Y = OUTSTANDING 45-25". We checked the arithmetic on each one and it adds up, but each covers a window the seller chose. His Last 20 table was very strong on 20 Nov 2026 at 16 wins and 4 losses, almost all of them overs, but it covers only five days.
An outside site, SportsHub, tracks the free picks he gives away on WagerTalk and showed them 6 and 0 over the last 30 days. That is encouraging but tiny, and it covers free plays only.

We found no independent post from anyone who bought his picks, good or bad, on any forum, review site or Reddit copy we checked. The CapperTek reviews of WagerTalk describe buyers losing after purchase, but none of them names him. Treat the numbers as marketing until you have tracked his picks yourself.

guarantee: WagerTalk sells many daily picks in two versions: a plain price and a higher "Guaranteed" price. The same site rule would apply to his daily picks, though none was on sale on 17 or 20 Nov 2026. The box on his profile says the guarantee "backs your purchase with 100% in credits." In its words, if your daily package "does not result in an overall profit across all included plays, the paid cash value of a guaranteed pick will be credited back to your account to be used on a future purchase." The credit can be spent on a daily package, a daily guaranteed package or any multiple day package. It is not cash back.

The WagerTalk refund policy names Wager Talk Media, LP as "the parent company of WagerTalk" and says "All Sales are Final and products are sold “as is”." It adds: "Once a product or service has been purchased, delivered, and/ or viewed, no refunds will be issued."

The terms say the seller is located at 11035 Lavender Hill Dr in Las Vegas, NV 89135, that the contract is governed by Nevada law, and that "Our company's entire liability, and the purchaser's exclusive remedy, shall be a refund of the price paid or replacement of our products" at the company's option. They also call the content "for entertainment and amusement purposes only."
We saw no guarantee on the multi day or season passes. Nothing covers losses on the bets themselves, which are usually far larger than the package price.

claims_note: How we checked: we recomputed every percentage on the profile from its own win and loss counts, counted the rows in the Last 20 table ourselves, and compared the Hot Streaks box on 17 Nov and 20 Nov 2026. The arithmetic is right in every case. That shows the figures are internally consistent; it does not show they are complete.

Each run covers a window the seller picked, such as the last nine weeks (L9W), the last six weeks of a season (L6W) or the last three years of playoffs (L3Y). None is a full season or career record. Units depend on how big each play was rated, and WagerTalk does not publish the full list behind the runs.

A quick sense check on the nine week run: 59.7% winners at standard -110 odds would return about 14% on money risked. The claimed 15.9% is close, which fits a mix of better prices or larger winning plays. It does not suggest the figure was inflated.

The 20 Nov Last 20 table was very one sided in style: 17 of the 20 plays were overs or over team totals, across college basketball, the NBA, the NFL, the CFL and college football. A buyer gets a lot of over bets, and a cold spell for overs would hit the whole card at once.

The bio says he was invited to the Stardust Invitational in 1996 and 2004 and the Sunset Station Invitational in 2000, and that his 1990s newsletter was carried by over 30 sportsbooks and the Gambler's Book Club. We did not find outside records to check these.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: very little. We found no full, time stamped log of every Rob Veno pick kept by a third party, no contest results we could open, and no court or regulator record about him.

What the seller publishes: a Last 20 table, a Hot Streaks box and Who's Hot leaderboards, all graded by WagerTalk, the company that sells the picks. On 20 Nov 2026 the Last 20 table showed 16 wins and 4 losses for 15 to 19 Nov. The all sports Who's Hot board ranked him first over 30 days at 87-66-2 and +$4,500 at $100 a play, and second over 3 days at 9-3. The NFL board showed him 16-8 over 30 days and 5-1 over 7 days, and the college basketball board 5-1 over 3 days.

One outside tracker: SportsHub, a pick tracking site that says it takes no sportsbook advertising, logs the free picks he posts on WagerTalk. On 20 Nov 2026 it showed 6 wins and 0 losses over the last 30 days (+$600 at $100 a pick), across college football, college basketball, the NBA, the WNBA and the CFL. Six free picks is far too few to judge anything, and free picks are not the paid card.

History: a saved copy of RobVenoSports.com from August 2020 called him one of the nation's elite "Big Play" handicappers, advertised "29 YEARS of SPORTS BETTING SUCCESS" and listed a Denver mailing address and an 800 number, with a 2019 copyright shared with a company called Sports Betting Today. The site answered until early 2023 and returned an error by January 2024. CapperTek still keeps an unclaimed, empty review page for RobVenoSports.com.

He also co hosts WagerTalk shows and podcasts, such as Full Court Press with Adam Trigger and an Every Game On The Board college football episode from November 2024. These show how he thinks, but they are not a record.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no pick history from Rob Veno is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Rob Veno performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the runs on his WagerTalk profile sit at about 57% to 64% winners. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence about Rob Veno is close to nonexistent. Most public posts that name him are WagerTalk's own announcements or forum rules. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: Across every place we looked we found no post from anyone who says they bought Rob Veno picks, positive or negative. That covers Covers, Sportsbook Review and TheRX through web searches, our saved copies of ten betting subreddits plus a scan of the newest r/sportsbetting and r/sportsbook posts, CapperTek (both the WagerTalk page and an empty page for his old RobVenoSports.com site), and the Better Business Bureau, which has no listing for WagerTalk. The posts that name him are WagerTalk free pick announcements, videos and podcasts, and TheRX daily threads that list him among services members may not repost. Fourteen CapperTek reviews of WagerTalk from 2021 to 2026 describe losing after purchase, and several call the whole site's records misleading, but none names him, so they speak to the marketplace rather than to his picks. With no posts either way there is no smoke to report; there is simply very little talk about him as a seller. Full text search in the Reddit archive kept timing out on 20 Nov 2026, so our Reddit check relied on the saved copies and the newest posts.

CapperTek lists 14 reviews of WagerTalk.com. They describe advertised records that did not hold up after purchase, reward points that were hard to use, and excuses after losing days; one says the reviewer followed six named WagerTalk cappers for almost four months and all lost overall. None of the 14 mentions Rob Veno.

TheRX daily service play threads tell members not to post picks from a list of services. The list starts with "All Wagertalk Cappers" and also names him. The thread gives no reason, and it is a forum rule, not a judgment on any one handicapper.
The same do not post list, with his name on it, appears in the 20 Oct 2026 thread, so the rule has stood for at least a month. We saw no member discussing his results in either thread.
CapperTek keeps a profile for his old site RobVenoSports.com marked "Unverified Service." It holds no reviews or complaints and no graded picks.
A Better Business Bureau search for WagerTalk returned no business, so there is no BBB complaint history for the company that sells his picks.
Web searches of Covers, Sportsbook Review and TheRX, and our Reddit copies, found no thread reviewing Rob Veno by name and no buyer posting a record of his paid picks.

conflicts: WagerTalk grades his picks, ranks him on its own leaderboards and sells his packages. The records on his profile therefore come from the seller's side of the deal.
He co hosts WagerTalk shows and podcasts, such as Full Court Press with Adam Trigger, and the free picks and shows double as advertising for paid passes.

WagerTalk's footer says it "participates in affiliate marketing programs" with gaming platforms and may be paid when readers use partner links or promo codes. It says this does not influence its picks.

Sportsmemo.com, which still lists him with copy from the 2018 to 2019 football season, uses the same WagerBuxx credits and Power Pass products as WagerTalk, so it is a sister storefront, not an independent source.
strengths: Sold through a company with a Las Vegas street address, a named parent company and written terms.
Every package has a published price, from $39 a day, with no hidden subscription.
A long, specific public history in Las Vegas betting media, partly confirmed by his own older website and years of WagerTalk shows and podcasts.
The Last 20 table shows losses as well as wins, and every percentage we recomputed matched its win and loss counts.
His free picks come with written reasoning, and an outside tracker logs them; that small sample was 6 and 0 over the last 30 days.
concerns: No full public record. Every number we saw is a run over a window chosen by the seller, or a ranking on WagerTalk's own board.
The guarantee pays in site credit, only on daily packages, never in cash. All sales are final.
We found no independent buyer reports, positive or negative, about his paid picks.
His years in the business are stated differently on different pages (29, 31 and 33), and a sister storefront still shows years old copy.
His recent card leans heavily on overs, so results can swing together when totals go cold.
TheRX bars members from reposting his plays, which removes one of the few places buyers might otherwise compare notes in public.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Check the Last 20 table and the Who's Hot boards on the day you buy, and note how they change over the next week.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and free days. Here it is site credit, only on daily packages.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get. Totals move fast.
Start with the cheapest pass that covers the sport you want rather than a year up front.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real, active WagerTalk handicapper with published prices, free picks and a company address behind the sales, and a long history on Las Vegas betting radio. We could not verify that his picks win over time, because the only full figures on show are graded by WagerTalk itself, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.

A Connecticut native who, per his bio, lived in Las Vegas from 1991 to 2002, co hosted a betting radio show from 1992, published a football and basketball newsletter in the 1990s and was part of Sportsmemo radio from 1998. He ran RobVenoSports.com for a time and joined WagerTalk in the summer of 2020. He now lives outside Philadelphia.
How much does Rob Veno cost?

On 20 Nov 2026 passes ran $39.00 for a day, $69.00 for three days, $99.00 for a week, $299.00 for 30 days, $749.00 for 90 days and $1,999.00 for a year. Season passes ran from $259.00 to $719.00, prop passes $199.00 or $499.00, and a one payment year promotion was $1,188.

No cash refunds. WagerTalk says all sales are final once a product is purchased, delivered or viewed. Guaranteed daily packages that do not profit return the price as site credit, and his passes carry no guarantee.
Does Rob Veno have a verified record?

No. His profile shows runs such as +71.7 units at 83-56-0 over nine weeks and a Last 20 table of 16 wins and 4 losses on 20 Nov 2026, all graded by WagerTalk. An outside tracker of his free picks showed 6 and 0 over 30 days. We found no independent, time stamped log of every paid pick.

For the money you get every play he releases in the period you buy, with written analysis, and his recent seller side numbers are good. What is unproven is whether his picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays. The guarantee only gives site credit on daily picks, and nothing refunds your betting losses.
